title: Chonyo, the Second Son of Shimon HaTzaddik
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Menachot 109b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.109b.13-16) relates that Shimon HaTzaddik, before his death, commanded that Chonyo his second son should serve in his place. Shimi his brother, who was two and a half years older than he, became jealous of him. Shimi said to him: “Come, I will teach you the order of the service.” He dressed him in a woman’s tunic (unkali) and girded him with her ribbon (tziltzol) and stood him by the altar, and Shimi said to his brother Kohanim: “See what this one vowed to his beloved and fulfilled …” The Kohanim wanted to kill him, and he fled to Alexandria in Egypt and built an altar there — the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehudah relates that the incident was that Chonyo did not accept it, and nonetheless Chonyo became jealous, etc.[^1]

In Josephus’s Jewish Antiquities it is related that Shimon HaTzaddik left a small son named Chonyo, and Elazar, Shimon’s brother, served in his place. Hyman identifies the Chonyo who built an altar in Egypt as the son of Shimon ben Chonyo ben Shimon HaTzaddik; Hyman therefore insists that the Gemara means Shimon, the grandson of Shimon HaTzaddik, and the name “HaTzaddik” became corrupted from the preceding story.[^2]
Hyman has already treated this at length in the entry Shimon HaTzaddik.

notes.text: The disguise appears in both Talmudic accounts. The brothers switch roles in Rabbi Yehudah’s version.

The linked Menachot gives two versions. In Rabbi Meir’s account Shimi is jealous, and in Rabbi Yehudah’s account Chonyo is jealous. The versions also differ in their descriptions of the Egyptian altar. Hyman uses Josephus to argue for a later generation and a corruption of the title HaTzaddik.
